Food and body

tángshí

dine in

recognition-first; the counter question since 2020 (tángshí háishi dài zǒu "for here or to go?").
Xiànzài néng tángshí le ma?

Can we dine in now?

chīlema

you eaten? (casual greeting)

classic hello, not a real question — answer Chī le, nǐ ne? and move on.
Chī le ma?

Chī la, nǐ ne? — Eaten yet? — Yep, you?

zhǎngpàng

to gain weight

zhǎng here is "grow" — same written word also read cháng "long (in length)"; you know them as two sounds.
Wǒ zhège yuè zhǎng pàng le

I've gained this month.

yǒudiǎnr

a bit (too)

erhua fused (yǒudiǎnr); tilts negative — yǒudiǎnr guì "a bit pricey".
Jīntiān yǒudiǎnr lěng

It's a bit cold today.

two readings — exasperated (wǒ zhēn fú le "I give up") or admiring (nǐ tài lìhai, fú le).

Glue — grammar

jiù vs cái

Template: Time + jiù/cái + Verb

jiù = earlier/sooner than expected ("already, as early as"); cái = later/less than expected ("only then, not until")

Wǒ bā diǎn jiù shuì le

"I was asleep by eight (early!)" / Tā shí'èr diǎn cái chī fàn. — "He didn't eat until noon (late!)"

reading them as plain "then" and missing the attitude

zài vs yòu

Template: future "again" = zài + Verb; past "again" = yòu + Verb + le

zài for next time, yòu for what already happened again

Xià cì zài lái a!

"Come again!" / Nǐ yòu chídào le! — "You're late again!"

promising with yòu (Wǒ yòu qù would mean "I went again")

Recall quiz

Sweep — known base (fast)

Hear it, see it: do you know it cold? No grading games.

Native notes — attitude particles and the intensity ladder

jiù and cái carry judgment, not just time

Wǒ bā diǎn jiù shuì le doesn't just report bedtime — it brags or confesses 'that's EARLY'. Tā shí'èr diǎn cái chī fàn grumbles 'finally, at noon'. Natives use them to editorialize constantly; a bare time statement with neither particle sounds robotic.

yòu…le is the eye-roll particle

Yòu lái le! ('here we go AGAIN') is the reflexive complaint frame — late friend, repeated excuse, boss's new idea. The le completes the resignation. zài is the hopeful twin: Xià cì zài lái (come again — future) can never swap with yòu.

The intensity ladder: hěn → tài…le → jí le → sǐ le

hěn is baseline (so neutral it's almost grammar), tài…le is enthusiastic, jí le is visceral (rè jí le — you can feel it), sǐ le is theatrical death (rè sǐ le — performative suffering, extremely common, rarely literal). Climb the ladder by relationship: sǐ le with friends, hěn/tài with colleagues.

Cultural: niúbī is a landmine with a safe twin

niúbī among close friends is high praise; at work or with elders it's a vulgarity that ends conversations. tài niú le is the socially safe version — same energy, no anatomical etymology. When in doubt, lìhai (impressive) never offends. And there is no tipping anywhere — the admiration word is the whole transaction.
